# ubertooth-one

> 2.4 GHz wireless development platform for Bluetooth monitoring

**Vendor:** Great Scott Gadgets

Status: **supported** — the identifiers and setup recipe are believed correct.

**Not maintainer-verified**: nobody on this project has run this hardware yet. The two facts are recorded separately on purpose (D-027) — a correct recipe and a tested device are different claims.

## What it is

An open-source 2.4 GHz platform built for observing Bluetooth Classic and Bluetooth Low Energy, which ordinary Bluetooth adapters cannot do.

## What you can do with it

Follow BLE connections, capture advertising traffic, and pipe results into Wireshark for analysis. spectools drives it as a raw 2.4 GHz spectrum sweep source too (its ubertooth_hw_u1.c matches 1d50:6002 and the old ffff:0004), a second use of the same hardware at no cost.

## Setup

Install the packages, add yourself to plugdev, log out and back in. Run ubertooth-util -v to confirm the firmware version matches the host tools — a mismatch is the usual cause of confusing behaviour.

## Known problems

Host tools and device firmware are versioned together and must match; Debian's ubertooth package and a device flashed elsewhere often disagree. Capture is best-effort by design — it is a monitoring platform, not a protocol analyser with guaranteed coverage.

## How it identifies itself

| USB id | What | Confirmed | Node |
|---|---|---|---|
| `1d50:6002` | Ubertooth One | yes | libusb |
| `1d50:6000` | Ubertooth Zero | yes | libusb |

## Access and permissions

Group membership required: `plugdev` — added at install, applies at next login.

The generated udev rule provides a `/dev/ubertooth` symlink, mode `0660`, group `plugdev`.
